title: BECE Business Studies: Book-keeping - Business Studies - Book-keeping: Introduction to Book-keeping
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The art of keeping accounts in a regular and systematic manner is known as:
questions.explain:
**Book-keeping** is the systematic and regular recording of financial transactions of a business. It ensures that there is a reliable and accurate record of income and expenditures.

> *Note the distinction:*

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| **Book-keeping** | The day-to-day systematic recording of financial transactions. |
| **Accounting** | The process of summarizing, analyzing, and interpreting those recorded transactions. |
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The following are reasons for keeping proper books of account EXCEPT:
options: determining the profit or loss of the business
determining the personal age of the business owner
providing permanent records of financial transactions
questions.explain: Proper book-keeping has several importance to a business, such as calculating profit/loss, acting as evidence of transactions, and providing tax information. It does **not** provide personal biological data like the age of the business owner, which is entirely irrelevant to the financial state of the enterprise.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is an essential quality of a good book-keeper?
questions.explain: A book-keeper must possess specific essential qualities to perform their duties efficiently. **Accuracy** is critical because errors in financial records can lead to substantial financial losses and misinformed decisions. Other qualities include *honesty*, *neatness*, and *punctuality*.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business uses its book-keeping records primarily to:
questions.explain: The primary **importance of book-keeping** is to provide management with accurate financial data needed to make informed and strategic decisions, such as whether to expand the business, cut costs, or take a loan.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Book-keeping is primarily concerned with the recording of business transactions that are expressed in terms of:
questions.explain: According to the **Money Measurement Concept** in accounting, book-keeping only records business transactions that can be assigned a definite monetary value (e.g., $₦10,000$, $\$50$). Sentiments, quality, and human effort are not recorded.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Common source documents used as evidence of a transaction in book-keeping include the following EXCEPT:
questions.explain: Common documents in book-keeping include *invoices*, *receipts*, *cheques*, and *vouchers*. A **medical report** is a health-related document and has no place as a source document for a business financial transaction.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A businessman lost his goods to a fire outbreak. Which importance of book-keeping will best help him claim compensation from his insurance company?
options: It prevents the business from going bankrupt
It provides documentary evidence of assets and stock lost
It increases the daily sales volume immediately
It helps to identify the exact physical cause of the fire
questions.explain: One of the key importance of book-keeping is that it **serves as documentary evidence**. In the event of a disaster, the insurance company will require documented proof of the assets and inventory that were lost before they can calculate and pay compensation.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A book-keeper who deliberately alters figures to steal money lacks the essential quality of:
questions.explain: **Honesty** (or integrity) is an essential quality of a book-keeper. Altering figures to commit fraud is a breach of trust and a severe ethical violation.
questions.subject: Business Studies
